# Emerald Green #1211: audit of south-facing hypothesis and surrounding heights

Updated 5 October 2026 after receiving the user's clearer #2111 screenshot and Claude's proposed landmark interpretation. This is an evidence update to DEEP_DIVE.md. The pasted Claude analysis is a claim to test, not an instruction or verified source. Its referenced claude/ report was not found in the active repo.

## Assessment

**Best working interpretation: line 11 probably has a south/SSW main exposure, about 209° true if its main window follows the complex's southward long wall. This remains an inference rather than owner confirmation.** The new screenshot makes the south hypothesis more persuasive than the earlier smaller video frame. Neither the receiving wing nor the exact window point has been established.

The main long footprint edges follow Manhattan's street grid. Taking the southeast wing's southward edge from local coordinates (13.8,-10.1) to (53.6,-32.1) yields a wall vector (39.8,-22.0) meters and a southwest outward normal at **208.93° true**. The opposite long wall points approximately29°. Bay-window angled panes have different aspects. Thus 209° is a geometrically coherent façade aspect, but the calculation alone cannot prove that #1211 occupies it.

## Landmark audit

- **Nearby right-hand tower: Townsend at 350 W37 / city tax-lot address352 W37 is plausible.** The [owner's gallery](https://townsendnyc.com/gallery/) photograph shows alternating light vertical piers, glass bays, and projecting horizontal bands consistent with the screenshot. It is west of Emerald Green with a recorded roof at284 ft /86.6m. Blinds prevent a unique exact match; its visible face may differ from the owner's street-facing photo. This remains a candidate, not an established landmark.
- **Distant glass tower: The Eugene is a better candidate than a confident One Manhattan West identification.** The screenshot has an angular/setback silhouette, tight horizontal floor grid, and dark rectangular area. [Beacon's dated construction photos](https://www.beacon.ws/news-events/beacon-news/nyc-construction-industry-news-one-manhattan-west-employs-unique-concrete-core-design-on-challenging-site) show The Eugene with a dark rectangular leasing panel and angular upper mass, while One Manhattan West's construction stages look materially different. [SLCE's project page](https://www.slcearch.com/project/the-eugene/) provides a completed façade comparison and describes730ft /62 stories. The screenshot's blinds and uncertain recording date prevent definitive identification. The crane is not reliably established in the supplied frame.
- Both candidates are on the southwest/west side, so even correcting the distant landmark could preserve the south/SSW hypothesis.
- Absence of Times Square towers in one framed/blinded view is weak negative evidence. A bay pane and camera can show only part of an exposure; intervening façades can hide expected landmarks.
- Upload date is not recording date. Visible construction cannot be used as proof of construction occurring now.

## All surrounding buildings

The existing inventory contains281 footprint records /281 distinct BINs within300m of reference point(-73.9932,40.755), all directions. The new companion CSV adds meters and distance/bearing sensitivity for two illustrative window sites. No site is asserted to be #1211. [Full inventory](heights_metric_and_position_sensitivity.csv). [Height map](surrounding_heights.png).

[NYC OTI Building Footprints](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/BUILDING/5zhs-2jue) supplies roof height; [DCP PLUTO](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/PLUTO/64uk-42ks) supplies tax-lot addresses. Roof heights are above each structure's own ground; these are not every setback elevation. An address can have multiple footprints with different heights. # Listening test for #1211 against a quiet Gotham West baseline

The user reports little noise in former apartment 300 at 550 W 45th Street. Floor and exposure are unconfirmed. That lived experience is a meaningful comfort benchmark, but it cannot calibrate decibels or isolate why Gotham West was quiet.

## What the complaints can mean inside the bedroom

| Source | Typical experience to listen for | Main uncertainty in #1211 |
|---|---|---|
| Trucks, private carting, deliveries | Intermittent engine rumble, acceleration, reversing signals, metal/bin impacts; a quiet interval followed by a sharp event | Exact curb/loading location, collection schedule, window seals, receiving elevation and screening |
| Horns / traffic | Short peaks above the traffic bed; potentially annoying at night even when average sound is modest | Window assembly and sightline to the roadway; a higher floor is not a guarantee |
| Music / voices | Often much quieter with windows shut; low bass can remain after intelligible voices disappear | Where the source actually is, frequency content, duration, and whether it is outdoors or another unit |
| Construction | Drilling/jackhammering, equipment or occasional impact; interior works can transmit through connected structure | Active phase, authorized hours, connection to this building and construction duration |
| Bedroom HVAC | Airflow whoosh, compressor start/stop, tonal hum, cabinet rattle or vibration | Actual equipment condition; building-wide manufacturer marketing is not a bedroom measurement |
| Neighbors / corridors | Voices versus footsteps, door slams or impact thumps | Adjacent occupancy and floor/wall details; street complaints do not measure partition isolation |

These are source descriptions, not claims that every sound is present in #1211. The 3D view model is not an acoustic model: visual screening does not quantify transmission, diffraction, reflection or structure-borne sound.

## A practical paired listening sequence

1. Start in the bedroom with windows fully shut and latched, HVAC off, no music/white noise. Listen at the intended pillow position and at the window. Note what is audible rather than only recording a single average number.
2. Briefly open a window, then latch it again. A large change helps distinguish exterior transmission from room equipment; it does not prove nighttime events will be inaudible.
3. Run low fan, then higher fan, then actual heating/cooling long enough to hear a compressor cycle. Compare whoosh, low hum, startup clicks and vibration separately. Switch it off again to avoid the fan masking street noise.
4. Listen at the quietest feasible nighttime opportunity, ideally spanning an actual collection/delivery event, plus a weekday morning construction period. A ten-minute quiet showing has little power to exclude intermittent overnight disturbances.
5. Record any obvious source, its start/end, window position, HVAC setting and room location. A phone recording is useful for repeat comparison, but phone processing and low-frequency limitations make it unsuitable for a confident prediction of sleep disturbance or a regulatory measurement.

Ask the leasing team for current collection/loading locations and hours, the exact bedroom window/HVAC specifications, and known nearby work. Asking for an observation or document is more useful than asking whether the building is simply 'quiet.' No request has been sent on the user's behalf.

## What a fix would actually address

A bad seal or latch is a concrete exterior-noise pathway to inspect. A rattling HVAC cabinet or excessive compressor vibration warrants equipment service. Curtains, rugs and wall absorption may reduce room echo, but cannot be assumed to block truck rumble or structural impacts. White noise adds masking sound; it does not reduce the source. Keep the HVAC intake, discharge and service/filter access clear when choosing the bed position.

## Primary sources

- [NYC DEP residential noise-control guidance](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/air/noise/residential-noise-control-guidance-sheet.pdf): source/path/receiver distinction, outdoor ingress, room absorption and equipment isolation.
- [NYC DEP interior HVAC guidance](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dep/downloads/pdf/air/noise/interior-hvac-noise-control-guidance-sheet.pdf): rotating equipment can transmit sound and vibration through a building; absorptive treatments address reverberation.
- [NYC 311 business-equipment complaints](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01935): DEP must observe a condition to issue a summons. Lack of an observed violation does not establish absence of intermittent sound.
- [Ice Air console operating manual](https://www.ice-air.com/wp-content/uploads/ICE6064-WSHP-CHPW-Manual.pdf), pp. 9–10: intake/discharge/filter access and excessive-noise servicing. Exact #1211 model remains unconfirmed.

The attached inventory covers **every retrieved footprint within 300 meters of the building reference point**, in all directions: **281 footprint records / 281 distinct BINs**. All have positive recorded roof heights; two could not be matched to a PLUTO address. This is a complete inventory within that boundary, not a claim to enumerate every distant skyline building or unrecorded construction project.

- [All 281 footprints: height, address, BIN, distance and bearing](surrounding_buildings_300m.csv)
- [Full-resolution map](surrounding_heights.png)

![Emerald Green surrounding roof heights](surrounding_heights.png)

The closest substantial structures are below. Bearings and directions are from a **building reference point**, not a surveyed #1211 window. Rounded heights are feet above each structure's own ground level. Distance is to the closest footprint edge, not across a particular window's sightline. Story counts are PLUTO tax-lot values, not measured heights of each roof or podium.

## What the noise evidence actually says

The building-lot query returned **50 noise service requests** submitted from 4 October 2023 through retrieval on 5 October 2026. They occur on **39 distinct submission dates**; **9 are explicitly described as duplicates**. There are **37 requests at normalized 320 West 38th Street**, plus one malformed “320W” address and 12 requests at other lot addresses. This lot covers aliases on both 37th and 38th Streets. These are requests, not independent incidents or unique residents.

| Reported source / descriptor | Requests | Implication |
|---|---:|---|
| Before/after-hours construction | 13 | Some submissions are overnight; authorization and actual work times are not established |
| Construction equipment | 8 | Worksite noise; temporary or episodic exposure is possible |
| Jackhammering | 6 | Distinctive impact noise; location coded to the lot, receiving apartment unknown |
| Music/party | 12 | Includes residential and street reports; does not prove an ongoing adjacent-neighbor problem |
| Banging/pounding | 5 | Includes three commercial reports at 310 W 38th on one date |
| Private carting | 1 | Sparse recent reporting cannot rule out routine pickup noise |
| Dog / HVAC / horn / engine idling / alarm | 1 each | Separate mechanisms requiring separate checks |

Construction accounts for **27 of 50 requests (54%)**. Complaint-type fields separately contain 9 residential, 5 street/sidewalk, 3 commercial, 2 vehicle and 31 generic DEP noise requests. Seventeen submissions were between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.; submission time is not necessarily the sound's occurrence time. Annual counts are 8 in the partial 2023 period, 6 in 2024, 23 in 2025, and 13 in 2026 to retrieval. These partial periods should not be treated as a clean year-over-year rate comparison.

The exact requests and agency responses are preserved in the [full ledger](NOISE_COMPLAINT_LEDGER.md), [CSV](noise_complaints.csv), and [official-source query](evidence/erm2-nwe9_query.txt). Source: [NYC 311 service requests](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/311-Service-Requests-from-2010-to-Present/erm2-nwe9).

### The episodes that matter most

**October–November 2023:** repeated equipment/jackhammer requests at 320. Several are marked duplicates. The private-carting request was submitted 22 November at 13:50, with an agency response later; it does not document a verified nightly pickup schedule.

**25 August–2 September 2025:** a cluster includes before/after-hours submissions at 23:37, 00:58 and 01:37, plus late-evening jackhammer requests and a 23:46 jackhammer submission on 2 September. Some are duplicates or generic closures. This is meaningful evidence that residents/reporters experienced episodes they considered disruptive overnight. It does not establish nightly noise across the whole period, a source directly beneath #1211, or a continuing October 2026 project.

**11 October 2025:** street music requests seven minutes apart, at approximately 22:54 and 23:01, received police-action responses. Treat these as a possible single episode rather than two independent bad nights.

**7–8 January 2026:** residential music reports at 320 and 318 received corrected-without-summons responses. No floor, apartment or affected neighbor is identified. The similar adjacent addresses should not be treated as proof of noise near line 11.

**11 April 2026:** six submissions at 310 W 38th include commercial banging at 02:53 and 02:59, construction before/after hours at 02:58, equipment and another after-hours request in the morning, and banging in the afternoon. Two commercial requests received corrected-without-summons responses. One DEP request is a duplicate; another closed because the complainant did not respond. This could represent a concentrated work/operating disturbance reported through multiple categories. The data do not name a tenant or contractor, so attributing it to a particular restaurant would be speculation.

**15 April 2026:** the latest construction-related request in the building-lot subset. **5 September 2026:** the latest noise request in that subset, banging/pounding at 339 W 37th, with no evidence observed by police at the visit. Thus the dataset does not show a continuously reported building-lot construction problem through September. Absence of requests does not demonstrate silence.

### Closed does not mean fixed

Agency responses include explicit duplicates, no violation found at a later inspection, generic “researched / could be closed,” no complainant response, inability to enter, action unnecessary, police action/correction, and a dog warning letter. These have different meanings. In particular, “no violation observed” is compatible with a short noise event having stopped before inspectors arrived. Police asking that a condition be corrected is stronger corroboration of an episode, but does not prove permanent resolution. No response or access failure is weak evidence about the underlying sound.

### Older reviews: useful descriptions, limited transfer to this unit

The [ApartmentRatings archive](https://www.apartmentratings.com/ny/new-york/emerald-green_212535050010018/) contains detailed 2012–2017 accounts of late-night metal-bin garbage collection, 37th Street tunnel-bound horns, construction, and hallway/neighbor noise. Some reviewers describe sleep interruption; other reviewers praise separation between apartments or say noise did not bother them. One explicitly locates their windows on 37th Street. Most do not identify floor, line, window condition, or whether windows were closed. Treat these as evidence of possible mechanisms rather than a current acoustic measurement of #1211. Historical construction accounts cannot establish today's work schedule, and hostile comments about groups of residents have no value for assessing sound transmission.

### Neighboring-address evidence

A separate 150-meter geographic query returned **708 noise requests** in the same period, including Emerald Green requests. It is neighborhood context, not 708 building complaints. Normalized address examples:

In particular, the 348 W 36th concentration mostly reflects historical alarm reporting rather than evidence of continuous present-day construction. Raw records and the exact geographic query are saved in evidence/nearby_noise_150m.json and evidence/nearby_noise_query.txt.

This corroborates that the street-noise mechanism is not mentioned solely in Emerald Green's decade-old reviews. It is still anonymous testimony from a different property, not proof of audibility in #1211.

## Construction sources: what can and cannot be connected

The [DOB NOW filings](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/DOB-NOW-Build-Job-Application-Filings/w9ak-ipjd) yield 13 filings for BIN 1087840:

- **M01074916-I1:** limited garage repairs, $66,000 initial cost, filed 3 October 2024; first permit 8 October 2024; signed off 4 February 2026; LOC Issued. This is a documented historical source candidate, not evidence of continuing garage work.
- **M00770323-I1 / P1:** first-floor commercial partition renovation at 310 W 38th; initial filing August 2022, with an amendment filed 12 June 2026 and approved 15 June 2026, $180,000 listed cost. The amendment is a live diligence lead, not a verified start date, remaining work schedule, or causal match to April's complaints.
- **M00976598:** place-of-assembly filing/amendments at 310, including a June 2025 approval. Approval does not identify the source of music or banging.
- **M00989156-I1:** January 2024 filing described as IRA to assist with FISP; sidewalk-shed filings also exist. These support asking about façade work, not asserting a current window-level noise problem.

I did not establish a permit/after-hours-variance match to the specific overnight complaint dates. Ordinary construction is generally allowed weekdays 7 a.m.–6 p.m.; after-hours authorization and emergency exceptions exist. Authorized work can still be noisy and can still be reported. Sources: [NYC311 construction guidance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01091), [DOB after-hours variance guidance](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/after-hour-variances-info.page).

## How these mechanisms could affect #1211

**Trash collection and truck impacts — meaningful sleep-risk lead.** Engine sounds and abrupt metal impacts are different from steady ambient traffic. A quiet daytime tour does not test a recurring midnight pickup. Direct visibility of the pickup area, shielding by another wing, façade openings and closed-window seals determine whether it is clearly audible. The old garbage accounts should trigger a pickup-location/schedule check, not an automatic rejection or dismissal.

**Traffic horns — especially important if the unit directly faces 37th.** If line 11 faces an internal court behind another wing, direct roadway exposure could be lower. Reflected sound and gaps can still transmit noise. If it directly fronts 37th, the historical street accounts transfer more plausibly. This is why locating the line on a full floorplate matters.

**Construction — episodic risk with a recent documented lead.** Noise near the façade or transmitted through the building structure can affect upper floors; “12th floor” alone is not a sufficient defense. The June 2026 commercial amendment warrants checking remaining demolition/drilling. Older 2023 construction reports should not be assumed ongoing. The current façade repair schedule remains an important open question from the earlier diligence.

**Music and neighbors — no established unit-specific pattern.** Nine residential requests across a 569-unit complex and several lot aliases do not identify a chronic problem next to #1211. Public records cannot establish the behavior of #1111, #1311 or the apartments beside #1211. Hallway sound through the entrance door is distinct from sound crossing the party wall or slab. The video also does not establish the bedroom-door condition in #1211.

**HVAC — test the unit itself.** The [equipment supplier's project sheet](https://www.ice-air.com/projects-data/pdfs/project-bios-165.pdf) identifies Ice Air water-source heat pumps at Emerald Green. The consoles beneath the windows should not automatically be described as ordinary through-wall PTAC units. That appearance alone does not establish an exterior sound-leak path. Check fan and compressor cycling, vibration, start/stop sounds, and operation separately in the bedroom and living room. Supplier claims of quiet operation do not demonstrate the condition of these particular installed units.

**Window construction and height:** energy-efficient or double-glazed does not mean acoustically excellent. [Pilkington's technical FAQ](https://www.pilkington.com/en-us/united-states-and-canada/architectural-and-technical-glass/product-categories/noise-control/noise-control-faq) explains that seals, glass specification and low-frequency performance matter. [FHWA guidance](https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/Environment/noise/noise_barriers/design_construction/design/design03.cfm) explains the importance of line-of-sight shielding. A higher floor may gain distance while losing shielding. Consequently I would not assign a decibel reduction between floors 12 and 21 or promise that the upper one is quieter from height alone.

## A concrete inspection that would change the decision

1. Obtain a marked north-oriented floorplate placing **#1211**, with both rooms and the other tower visible. Ask whether it directly faces 37th, 38th, or the internal court. Verify using a live window view rather than a representative listing photo.
2. Tour **actual #1211** with blinds raised and lights off. Photograph straight ahead and each angled bay pane. Note the closest building, approximate separation, visible sky at seated eye level, and privacy at the bed location. A 21st-floor substitute is insufficient.
3. With windows latched, stand quietly in the bedroom with HVAC off, then operate HVAC through low/high and a complete start/stop cycle. Listen near window seals and the entrance door. Check that the bedroom door closes and latches.
4. Identify the current garbage pickup location(s), whether bins are rolled under these windows, residential versus commercial pickup times, loading/garage routes and the remaining ground-floor renovation and façade schedule. Request the relevant noise mitigation plan/AHV details for any planned overnight work.
5. Observe the street and, if access can be arranged, the actual bedroom during **roughly 11 p.m.–1:30 a.m.**, reflecting the historical pickup complaints. A second early morning or rush-hour visit tests a different source. No single quiet interval proves every night quiet, but it is much more informative than a mid-afternoon tour.

**Decision:** I would keep it on the shortlist for space, layout and inexpensive amenities. I would not sign based on the #2111 view or assume the noise issue is solved because requests are closed. The unresolved facts that could materially change the value are the window-side placement, #1211's close façades/sky opening, nighttime pickup audibility, HVAC behavior and remaining construction schedule. There is enough evidence for targeted due diligence; there is no defensible public-source conclusion yet that this particular bedroom is quiet or that it receives an open south-facing view.

## Building, owner and amenities

A [2017 NYC financing document](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hyic/downloads/hyic-2017ab-os.pdf) lists Emerald Green with a 20-year 421-a tax exemption. HCR's older building lists also include the address. These are meaningful building-level signals; they do not establish #1211's exact present lease status or the exemption's end date.

Request a written statement of #1211's stabilization status, legal regulated rent, any preferential rent, complete vacancy rider, and 421-a benefit/surcharge schedule. [HCR explains](https://hcr.ny.gov/surcharges-and-fees) that certain older 421-a programs permit separately disclosed surcharges during benefit phase-out, using a specific historical rent basis. **Do not simply add 2.2% of $5,021.** Ask whether the advertised number already includes any surcharge and whether a charge changes during the initial lease. [HCR records access](https://hcr.ny.gov/node/9991) generally belongs to the subject tenant/owner or an authorized representative; request an owner-provided certified apartment history before signing rather than assuming prospective-tenant access.

Openigloo's generalized Good Cause badge was not adopted as a unit-specific legal conclusion. The actual exemption/status and lease documents govern.

The [2016 DOJ consent decree](https://www.justice.gov/d9/glenwoodsettle_2_11_16.pdf) lists Emerald Green among additional properties in Glenwood's accessibility case. [DOJ's case summary](https://www.justice.gov/crt/case/us-v-glenwood-management-corp-sd-ny) describes audits and proposed retrofits beyond Liberty Plaza. This is historical accessibility context, not evidence of an unresolved violation in #1211 today. No claim is made that the accessible public feeds capture every private lawsuit.

1. Is #1211 still available for October 16, and what is the ordinary-month total? Resolve $5,021 versus $5,022 and gross versus net wording.
2. Does its bedroom fully close with a permanent door? Send current continuous video, dimensioned plan, usable interior area and compass exposure.
3. Which supplied photos/video depict #1211? Show open-blind daylight views, appliances and any wear or planned refurbishment.
4. What are all mandatory charges and the gym/pool/lounge membership price? Is fitness alone free? Provide hours, guest rules and closure plans.
5. What is its rent-regulation status, legal rent, preferential rent if any, 421-a surcharge and benefit expiry? Is every collectible charge included in the quote?
6. Provide the current bedbug disclosure and latest annual filing. Any recent incidents in #1211, adjacent units or the same floor?
7. What garage/facade repairs remain? Any scaffolding, noise, roof closure or planned work facing #1211? Provide dates rather than verbal assurances.
8. How does its bedroom face refuse pickup, loading docks, restaurants, mechanical plant or construction? When are collections?
9. Confirm heating/electric/AC billing, internet providers and typical recent utility bills for this unit/line. What maintenance or equipment replacement is scheduled?
10. Will the employment offer letter meet income verification? Is remote touring/application allowed, and is a guarantor needed? Confirm deposit, insurance, application and move-in terms.

> I am interested in Emerald Green #1211 for an October 16 start. Please send an itemized written quote including all mandatory charges, any concession and any 421-a surcharge, plus the gym/pool membership options. StreetEasy shows $5,021 and your listing ID 6831 shows $5,022; please confirm the collectible monthly total. Please also send current video of #1211 showing the bedroom door closing, open-blind window views, washer/dryer, interior square footage and exposure; confirm the rent-stabilization status and provide the lease riders, current bedbug disclosure and any remaining facade/garage work schedule. Can my employment offer letter support approval before my start date, and can I tour and complete the process remotely?

**Decision rule:** tour promptly if they can document privacy and cost. Proceed only if the actual bedroom is quiet enough for sleep, the daylight/view suits you, and total rent plus selected amenities fits your budget. Reconsider if they cannot establish the bedroom enclosure, itemize collectible charges, or disclose scheduled disruptive work.

Obtain a complete quote listing every required recurring, usage-based, optional and move-in/out charge: amenities, package/trash/utility billing, internet, insurance, pets, bike/storage, reservation and moving fees. The application/deposit/electricity disclosures do not prove that every situational charge is zero. Ask whether October 15 possession is accepted and whether rent starts earlier. Current availability alone does not answer that.

## A focused inspection of 23J

1. **Inspect the exact apartment.** Confirm the number, current video/photo provenance and condition; measure usable bed/desk/sofa clearances, column and hallway. The combined living/kitchen plan dimensions are not a separate clear living-room measurement.
2. **Test systems.** Run HVAC at different settings, check vent airflow and bathroom exhaust, operate faucets/shower simultaneously, and test washer/dryer and dishwasher. Ask specifically about 24J's ventilation complaint and winter heat/hot-water repairs. Record observed noise/odors without assuming their source.
3. **Listen and smell.** Spend quiet time in each room with windows closed, HVAC off then on; listen for hum, alarms, traffic/horns, neighbors and door slams. Inspect floor-23 corridor and refuse room for smoke and cleanliness.
4. **Check service operation.** Ride elevators at a busy time, note waits, inspect posted certificates, and ask how many passenger cars serve floor 23. Observe guest verification, package logging and after-hours repair handling.
5. **Inspect shared facilities.** Test gym equipment and see rooftop/lounge condition, access rules, charges and planned closures. Confirm how commercial-tenant visitors and deliveries are separated from residents.
6. **Document defects.** Obtain a signed move-in condition record with photographs of floors, counters, bathroom fixtures, mirrors, appliances and windows. Get promised repairs and completion dates in writing.
7. **Walk your daily routes.** Test weekday/evening transit, groceries and waterfront access. Your comfort with the street and its traffic is more useful than a broad neighborhood safety label.

## Written answers that would clear the main concerns

- Who is today's legal landlord/operating manager, when did the team change, and who handles deposit accounting and escalated repairs?
- What resolved complaint 14859364 in 24J? Does its ventilation share equipment/riser with 23J? What complaints or water/pest incidents have affected 23J and adjacent units?
- Provide the current one-year bedbug disclosure, latest annual receipt, and post-November-2025 incident/treatment information. [HPD explains required disclosure](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/bedbugs.page).
- Provide accepted correction documentation for the five active elevator entries, any associated physical repairs and the last 12 months' outage history.
- What façade work remains under the SWARMP filing, with what schedule and effect on windows, scaffolding, roof access and noise?
- Confirm 23J's full pricing, lease/riders, legal and charged rent, renewal basis, tax-benefit notices, all fees, delivery date and current amenity terms.
- Provide surrounding-work notices, past storm/water-entry history and the building's backup-power/elevator outage plan.

Discuss directly with at least two current residents if possible, preferably on higher floors/J-line, about the last winter, summer HVAC, repair turnaround, smoke, elevator waits and the present team. Such conversations were not conducted for this research.

## Evidence boundary

No 23J-specific adverse entry was found in the retrieved HPD data; this is not a clean bill of health. There are two closed HPD tenant-action cases and eight recorded executed evictions, none identified as 23J; counts lack the underlying dispute context and are not themselves evidence of wrongful conduct. Historical worker-injury owner litigation was found but does not establish current residential defects. Generic 311 and targeted OATH/FDNY cases were checked in the supplemental appendix; full FDNY inspection files, a complete court-docket/ownership-title audit, environmental measurements and current unit/system inspection remain incomplete. Exact records and limitations are preserved in the linked appendices.

**Decision rule:** Proceed if 23J passes a weekday systems/noise/odor inspection, current residents support the service claims, and management supplies coherent written answers and lease terms. Pause if it refuses the current disclosures/compliance information, minimizes the nearby ventilation complaint without a repair explanation, or the exact unit has persistent smoke, poor airflow, mechanical noise or water damage. The evidence supports a conditional candidate; it does not support either automatic rejection or unconditional reassurance.

# Henry Hall: supplemental 311 and enforcement checks

Retrieved September 30, 2026. This supplements the official records appendix; that appendix's statement that generic 311 was outside its packet remains accurate for that packet, but the consolidated research now includes this separate check.

## 311 service requests, 2017–September 2026

Primary sources: [2010–2019 historical dataset](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/76ig-c548), restricted to records from 2017 onward, and [2020–present dataset](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/erm2-nwe9). Exact query URLs and complete results are saved in `records/311_2017_2019_query.txt`, `records/311_2017_2019.json`, `records/311_2020_present_query.txt` and `records/311_2020_present.json`.

The query matches Manhattan plus BBL1007107501 or relevant building alternate addresses:509/511/513/515/517 West38 and512 West39, with additional38th spelling variants in the current query. BBL catches several spacing variants in street labels. It does not capture every incident geocoded to an adjacent intersection or a wrong/missing address/BBL. This is building-parcel/address coverage, not a neighborhood-radius or crime-rate analysis.

Returned **277 unique service requests**,51 for2017–2019 and226 for2020–present, ranging February12 2017 to September11 2026. Seven records are in2017 and some predate the reported April2017 building opening. **275 Closed and2 In Progress**. The two in-progress records concern a July2026 damaged street tree and an August2026 food-establishment complaint; neither is an unresolved apartment maintenance finding.

Selected categories:

| Category | Requests | Meaning and limit |
|---|---:|---|
| Noise – Residential |50| Allegations at a building/address, not necessarily23J or50distinct neighbors/incidents |
| Other Noise |23| Construction, barking dogs, alarms and other equipment categories; not all residential apartment noise |
| Noise – Vehicle |6| Horn/vehicle complaints; source may be street traffic |
| Noise – Commercial |2| Commercial-use reports; no inference of audibility23J |
| Heat/hot water |36| Overlaps HPD's complaint feed; do not add36toHPD58as independent complaints |
| Encampment |33| Street/sidewalk reports, potentially repeated reporting of one condition; does not establish33criminal events or danger |
| Illegal parking |20| Street operations context |
| Smoking |3| Reported conditions, not a finding that the building's policy is unenforceable |
| Water leak |3| Overlaps housing complaint evidence; no23Jdetermination |

Among the35 residential-noise requests in2020–present,20 closure descriptions say police took action to fix the condition,7 say no evidence observed,6 say action unnecessary,1 says outside jurisdiction,1 says no access. Closure reasons differ. The last residential-noise entries in that period are May2025; the current query has two2026general-noise construction entries and no2026residential-noise entries. Absence of a recent report does not prove quiet.

Two particularly recent noise reports:

- **69893963, July30 2026,07:18:** construction before/after hours at515W38; closedAugust12 after DEP reported no Air/Noise Code violation observed at inspection. Not proof that the complaint was fabricated, nor proof of an ongoing violation.
- **68379775, March19 2026,23:29:** before/after-hours construction at515W38; closedMarch20 as duplicate of a previously filed complaint. The duplicate status does not establish resolution of the original source.

The2020–present feed includes isolated air/indoor-air quality, water/sewer/elevator, public-safety and animal complaints alongside trees, parking and collections. Their presence does not identify current unit defects or establish a building/area crime rate. Caller identities and motivations are unavailable. No building-specific population exposure, reporting propensity or comparable-building benchmark was derived.

**Practical consequence:** weekday acoustic testing, a walk of the street frontage and direct questions about reported noise/HVAC complaints are supported by both tenant narratives and public complaint records. The total request count is not a defensible building-quality score.

## OATH enforcement / FDNY

The official [OATH Hearings Division Case Status](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/jz4z-kudi) was queried using violation-location ZIP10018 plus the building's house/street aliases or block710/current and predecessor lots. Full response and query are `records/oath_address.json` and `records/oath_address_query.txt`. Metadata identifies this as the official OATH feed; a search-discovered community-created FDNY view was not used as enforcement authority.

The location query returned114records, including predecessor-site and undated entries. **64 have violation dates on/after April1 2017**, used as an approximate opening-period cutoff, not a proof each event occurred after occupancy. Of those, **14 FDNY records** are returned:7 unnecessary/unwarranted-alarm cases,3 recordkeeping,2 portable extinguishers/fire hoses,1 general maintenance,1 documentation. **All14 are marked All Terms Met**;13 hearing outcomes are In Violation and1 Dismissed. Several concern former commercial tenant Legacy Records, not residential apartment systems. The alarm cases name the owner/board; the latest is ticket012167945R, February22 2025, All Terms Met/balance0. This is a reason to ask about nuisance alarms and current system maintenance, not proof of an unsafe current fire system or linkage to a reviewer's in-unit buzzing noise.

All13 returned cooling-tower/DOHMH entries dated2017/2018 are **Dismissed / All Terms Met**. Allegation descriptions are not findings of Legionella contamination or actual drinking-water illness; no such condition is established here.

Outstanding status/financial entries are mainly **third-party vehicle-idling cases** at the street frontage, rather than fines against residential management. Do not attribute every parcel-address ticket to the landlord. One contractor case needs a specific cross-feed qualification: OATH ticket**035657100L**, August8 2022, names Benchmark Builders and records Defaulted / Penalty Due / balance$6,250. DOB ECB's corresponding**35657100L** records RESOLVE, certificate accepted and balance0 for the tenant-protection-plan violation. These are different agency status/financial fields; this research does not adjudicate the discrepancy or describe that contractor penalty as the landlord's unpaid debt. Accepted physical compliance and OATH financial outcomes must be distinguished.

This is a targeted OATH/FDNY-case lookup, not the complete FDNY inspection/history file or a certification of fire safety. ZIP/address/block variants, missing data, entity names and nonpublic inspection records limit coverage. Historical location records were not pooled into a current-risk score.

# Henry Hall: reviews, ownership and lease questions

Checked September 30, 2026. Public allegations are not adjudicated facts. No residents or management were contacted.

## Current ownership changes the interpretation of older reviews

[JLL's March 3, 2026 transaction announcement](https://www.jll.com/en-us/newsroom/jll-capital-markets-arranges-129m-sale-and-71m-financing-of-henry-hall) identifies Amstar Group LLC as buyer for $129 million, Shorenstein Investment Advisers/Dreamscape Companies as sellers, and $71 million in acquisition financing through U.S. Bank. This is a transaction participant's primary announcement, not an audited assessment of operating quality. The loan does not establish financial distress.

[Current StreetEasy building information](https://streeteasy.com/building/henry-hall) identifies Canvas Property Group as management/marketing/leasing team. Current listings call Canvas the landlord's exclusive broker/agent. Review platforms and older HPD registration records still identify Greystar. Obtain the actual current operating manager, legal landlord, management start date and deposit-accounting contact in writing. A sale does not prove either improvement or deterioration.

## Google Maps: directly inspected in the browser

[Henry Hall Apartments public Google Maps profile](https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ7QDM00xYwokRcAS3k4AlkfU) at 515 W 38th was opened through Google Maps search. The profile displayed **4.3/5 from 111 reviews**: 82 five-star, 10 four-star, 2 three-star, 2 two-star and 15 one-star. Thus 17/111, about 15.3%, were one- or two-star ratings; this is the share of posted reviews, not the share of unhappy residents. Google explicitly labels reviews unverified. The newest view and lowest-rating view were inspected, including the 15 one-star and 2 two-star entries loaded in that order; selected longer reviews were expanded. This was not a census of all 111 full texts.

Material allegations, using the relative dates actually shown by Google:

| Reviewer (names withheld) | Displayed age/rating | Relevant allegation | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reviewer A | Six months ago; 1 star | Deposit still unreturned after a long period; repeated follow-ups referred to accounting | Recent publication, but claimed events span years; responsible ownership period unknown |
| Reviewer B | Six months ago; 1 star | Deposit delayed; emails/calls unanswered | A second deposit allegation; no accounting records inspected |
| Reviewer C | One year ago; 1 star | Persistent buzzing/alarm sound inside unit and ineffective maintenance response | Test for mechanical hum in 23J; owner's reply said investigation was underway, not that repair was complete |
| Reviewer D | Two years ago; 1 star | Smoke infiltration, slow repairs and gym access for an outside trainer's clients | Lease/use-policy questions; reviewer's statement about smoking law is not adopted as legal fact |
| Reviewer E | Four years ago; 1 star; text refers to February–June 2022 | Bedbugs and delayed/disputed treatment, plus weekday drilling | Historical infestation allegation; official annual report separately establishes two infested units in the corresponding reporting period, not every detail of the allegation |
| Reviewer F | Five years ago; 1 star | Packages allegedly misplaced and found later | Older operational allegation, not proof of current theft |
| Reviewer G | Edited four years ago; 1 star | Disputed $1,200 charge for a bathroom mirror allegedly missing at move-in | Photograph and jointly record existing defects before possession |
| Reviewer H | Two years ago; 2 stars; claims three years' residency | Repairs, visitor access and service complaints; also praises broad triple-pane windows for outside-noise control | Some narrative claims are uncorroborated; no criminal allegation is treated as established |
| Reviewer I | Three years ago; 2 stars | Drafty windows, floors and slow washer/dryer in an affordable apartment | Do not transfer that unit's appliances or conditions to 23J |
| Reviewer J | Four years ago; 3 stars | Alleged 28% renewal increase after assurances of a reasonable increase | Cannot derive 23J's future increase or legal status from this; distinguish gross/legal rent, concessions and preferential rent |

Several low ratings concern unsuccessful tours or contain no narrative. They are weaker evidence of actual living conditions. The newest three entries were ratings without narratives: 5 stars two weeks ago, 5 stars one month ago, 4 stars one month ago. More substantive favorable reviews praise staff, maintenance, windows, layouts and cleanliness, but often predate the sale. A favorable staff experience and an unfavorable accounting/repair experience can both be real.

## Other review platforms: concise evidence checks

[ApartmentRatings](https://www.apartmentratings.com/ny/new-york/henry-hall-apartments_9199332346275178882/) shows 4.2/5, 36 reviews, 26 marked verified. Its verification includes surveyed prospects, not only established residents. September 2025 feedback praises service and window sound insulation; March 2025 reports shared-space upkeep/disorganization; August 2024 criticizes gym equipment. An August 2024 negative review alleges smoke and poor management. Older positive feedback is plentiful. Do not count cross-posted resident reviews as independent corroboration.

[Openigloo](https://www.openigloo.com/building/nyc/1090727-1007107501/manhattan-chelsea-515-west-38-street-10018) shows 4.1/5 from only five reviews and 60% recommendation/owner approval. Reports mention train horns, neighbor/dog noise, smoke, HVAC and visitor/package security. Its displayed relative review timestamp is unstable, so no precise publication date is inferred. Its headline says one open violation while the class breakdown is all zero; it says no litigation/bedbug history despite positive official historical records. These summaries cannot replace primary records.

[Birdeye](https://reviews.birdeye.com/henry-hall-apartments-156775759157076) shows 4.2/154 aggregated reviews, inconsistent with the directly inspected current Google count; treat it as an older/different snapshot. [RentCafe](https://www.rentcafe.com/apartments/ny/new-york/henry-hall/default.aspx) and [Point2Homes](https://www.point2homes.com/US/Apartment-Buildings/NY/New-York/Henry-Hall.html) display a management-company score based on approximately 17,800 reviews across properties. That is not Henry Hall's resident sample. Search results for Princeton and Western Michigan Henry Hall dorms were excluded.

## Commercial tenants and amenities

[Indienne's own site](https://www.indiennenyc.com/about) confirms its restaurant on Henry Hall's second floor. Old references to Legacy Records room service should be reconfirmed. Restaurant convenience is a benefit; separate resident access, visitor routing, trash/loading, odors, events and any resident discounts require current confirmation. Restaurant activity does not establish noise in a 23rd-floor unit.

The [building amenities page](https://henryhallnyc.com/amenities/) advertises a jam room, fitness center, rooftop and social spaces. Verify operational condition and access terms. A historical listing for [15F](https://streeteasy.com/property/9854960-henry-hall-15f) advertises stabilization and no amenity fee; that is useful context but not a current 23J promise.

## Regulatory and economic questions

[2019 Manhattan Community Board 4 material](https://www.nyc.gov/html/mancb4/downloads/pdf/november-2019/29-updates-to-mcb4-affordable-housing-plan-no-memo.pdf) identifies 225 apartments including 46 affordable units and permanent affordability for that component. [FY2018/19 DOF 421-a list](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/finance/downloads/pdf/421a/1819/421a_1819_manhattan.pdf) lists 509 W38 condominium lots 1304 (179 residences) and 1305 (46 residences). These are historical building-level evidence, not 23J's current regulatory determination or benefit-expiration date.

Ask for 23J's current rent-stabilization rider or written basis for exemption, legal regulated rent versus actual preferential/base rent, concession treatment at renewal, any 421-a expiration notice/surcharge and its calculation, and one-/two-year lease terms. HCR explains [tax-benefit regulation](https://hcr.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2022/07/fact-sheet-41-07-2022.pdf) and [surcharges](https://hcr.ny.gov/surcharges-and-fees); their applicability here remains unverified. Owners can furnish [certified apartment rent histories](https://hcr.ny.gov/node/9991); a prospective renter cannot assume unrestricted access to another tenant's records.

## Historical owner litigation

Official published decisions identify construction-worker injury litigation involving HY 38 Owner LLC: [Lima, September 14, 2022](https://www.nycourts.gov/courts/AD2/Handdowns/2022/Decisions/D69712.pdf), involving an alleged April 2015 caisson-pipe injury, and [Rodriguez, March 10, 2021](https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/3dseries/2021/2021_01436.htm), involving a construction-site gate injury. These concern construction work and procedural liability issues. They do not establish current unsafe residential conditions, a tenant judgment or a defect in 23J. Name searches are not a complete NYSCEF/eCourts docket audit, and entity association alone cannot identify every suit's property.

## What the evidence supports

Retain 23J as a serious candidate, with conditions. Review evidence is mixed rather than uniformly bad. The meaningful recurring checks are responsive maintenance/accounting, smoke control, security procedures, and actual acoustic performance. Verify the present team and exact unit instead of relying on the lobby, average rating, a generic no-fee advertisement or an older tenant's unit.

Research checked October 14, 2026, building on an October 8 comparison of Paramount Tower against other

## The building

- 52 storeys, 464 apartments, built 1997 (PLUTO). Managed by Glenwood. [Building page](https://www.glenwoodnyc.com/properties/midtown-east/paramount-tower/)

  (closed) in the record window; the latest bedbug filing (November 2024 to October 2025) reports 3 infested
  units, all eradicated, none reinfested. About 277 noise complaints a year within 150 m, 55% logged
  10 pm to 6 am; 8 heavy-construction filings on the block (demolition on East 38th Street).
- An earlier building review found a very clean city record and a few positive resident reviews, but a thin
  sample. It suggested asking about renewal increases, amenity or gym fees, and Second Avenue and
  Queens-Midtown Tunnel traffic noise inside the unit.

## The plan: E line, floors 3-27

Glenwood publishes one drawing per line and floor band. The E-line drawing for floors 3-27
([PM3-27E](https://glenwoodadmin.com/webdav/images/floorplans/paramount/PM3-27E.jpg)) prints:

| Room | Printed size |
|---|---|
| Living room | 23'0" x 12'5" |
| Bedroom | 16'6" x 11'4" |
| Kitchen | 7'9" x 7'2" |

Printed rooms add up to about 528 sq ft. Traced at the printed sizes, the whole apartment is about
690-740 sq ft of interior floor (715 used in the score, basis "same-line plan"). This is an estimate, not an
advertised size. The plan shows a walk-in closet, a coat closet and a foyer closet, a separate kitchen open to
the living room over a breakfast ledge, and angled bay windows in both rooms. **No washer/dryer is drawn**,

walk-through.

The floor plan file (`plans/paramount-tower-25e.json`) carries two furniture presets that fit with no
blocked or tight pieces: bed on the living-room partition with a 65-inch TV about 9 ft from the pillows, or
bed on the outside wall with a desk beside the column.

## Light and view

No source states which way the E line faces, and the plan has no north arrow. The 3D site model

| Fact | Effect |

| Gross rent, free months and lease term | Cost is 20% of the score and counts as neutral while unknown. |
| Monthly and one-time fees (amenity, gym, pool, move-in) | Needed for the true monthly cost. |

| Window direction | Lets the 3D sun study count instead of the floor-only estimate. |
| Lease start date | Fills the move-date fit. |
